variable_coverage.construction: Link restatement event and original-period fields to the original financial statements/firm-year. Code one for a qualifying subsequent restatement in the Audit Analytics vintage through 2011-10-20; keep original fiscal-year/issue-year and later restatement event date distinct.
For each original auditor engagement office and fiscal year, count U.S. SEC registrants using the paper-defined Big 4 office and client-year population.
Natural log of full-sample client total assets for fiscal-year t; local matched assets are candidates and do not verify the full-sample field or unit mapping.
Code one when full-sample client net income is negative in fiscal-year t; use the same vendor/population and timing as SIZE.
Follow Table 4 note: code one when the client changes auditor in fiscal year t. The methods text instead describes a restatement within the first year of a change; preserve the conflict as blocking.
Natural log of the official 2000 Census MSA population matched to the auditor’s office city. The population table is available; historical city-to-MSA matching remains unverified.
Code one when the historically assigned auditor office city differs from each of the twelve paper-listed SEC regional-office cities.
Natural log of annual client audit fees in fiscal year t; ensure the applicable fiscal-year convention and currency/units match the paper.
Natural log of annual client nonaudit fees in fiscal year t; Table 4 variable label NON_AUDIT is called NONAUDIT in its note.
Divide client audit plus nonaudit fees by total annual fees generated by SEC registrants in the auditor practice office; the full office-year denominator requires a separate population universe.
For each industry-year, code one for the national number-one Big 4 auditor based on aggregated audit fees using two-digit SIC. Exact ranking universe and full coverage are unresolved.
For each city-industry-year, code one for the number-one Big 4 office by aggregated client audit fees; exact ranking universe and office mapping remain unresolved.

design_coverage.reason: Historical company-to-restatement, auditor-at-original-issuance and engagement-office assignment is unverified.
Fiscal year, 2-digit SIC, Big 4 firm and SEC regional-office effects are reported; historical SIC coverage and office-city-to-period mapping remain unresolved.
One joint auditor-office-year cluster is reported; its historical membership keys must align to the unverified office assignments.
No weights are reported for this probit.
Probit is reported for binary RESTATEMENT; the standard-error procedure is joint auditor-office-year clustered.
Requires logged assets/fees, paper-defined fiscal-year alignment, 2000 MSA population mapping, office-year and fee rankings; relevant mappings/benchmark populations remain unresolved.

implementation_issues.description: AUDITOR_CHANGE conflicts: research-design text says a restatement occurs within the first year of an auditor change, while the selected Table 4 note says a client changes its auditor in year t. The Table 4-specific note is retained for the frozen baseline, but the conflicting construction is essential.
The exact 23,190 full-sample firm-year roster and complete screen cannot be verified from reported aggregate counts; the sample explicitly includes smaller firms not covered by Compustat.

The original-statements issuance-year auditor, restatement event and later event date require a historical link and an Audit Analytics data vintage frozen as of 2011-10-20. The local probe does not verify either.

The full-sample assets/net-income, fees and engagement-office relationships require the Audit Analytics full population. Matched Compustat values or a fee extract cannot establish this sample or its benchmark universes.
The auditor-office city to 2000 Census MSA mapping for LnPOPULATION and to the paper-listed SEC regional-office cities for SEC_REG_FAR/FE remains unverified.

Historical two-digit SIC coverage for the full firm-year sample and the national/city-industry fee-ranking benchmark universe is unverified; the frozen catalog/probes do not confirm the required population.

The national and city-industry leadership indicators require the paper’s ranking universe and all aggregated fee observations. The article does not provide a frozen benchmark roster or complete local coverage confirmation.
The client fee / office SEC-registrant fee ratio requires a complete office-year denominator and dated fee-to-office links; neither is confirmed by the local probe.

review_notes: The frozen baseline is Table 4 full sample (N=23,190); Table 4 reduced sample (N=17,842) and its Compustat/CRSP-only controls are not included.
Table 4’s AUDITOR_CHANGE note is retained while the conflicting methods definition is flagged as a blocking specification issue.

The event outcome is assigned to original financial-statement fiscal/issuance periods, while the restatement filing/event is later; the database cutoff is 2011-10-20 and must not be treated as sample fiscal year 2011.

Current local Audit Analytics metadata/probes show selected tables and fields only. No coverage confirmation establishes population, original-vintage history, office-year benchmark coverage or identifier mapping.
For the Census population input, the official 2000 MSA population table is available as public raw data, but assigning each auditor-office city to an MSA remains unresolved.
